newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steadied by unexpected weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steadied by unexpected weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices stayed relatively unchanged Monday in lackluster activity, steadied by unexpected forecasts for colder East Coast weather this week and next, industry sources said.
"I don't see any meteoric rise in prices, but the cold weather won't hurt," said a cash trader, noting better demand should help trim bloated stocks and tighten the balance.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent was still quoted in the $18.00-18.25 a barrel range. February paper was talked down a quarter or more to $17.60-85, with March off a similar amount to $17.50-75 on weaker crude, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was unchanged in the low-$19 area.
Traders said reports that a New England and New York utility may soon tender for additional one percent and 0.3 percent material, respectively, helped steady low sulphurs.
High sulphurs in New York again were flat from Friday.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was still pegged at about $16.50, while three percent was down slightly to $14.75 or lower, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
Cold weather in the East boosted New York city gate gas prices by about 15 cents to the $3.50/mmBtu level. NYH one percent resid remained at a $2.88/mmBtu equivalent.
